home.overviewquote: Children, love God with all your heart and show that love through sacrifice.
home.overviewdesc1: The Congregation of the Sisters of Saint Mary Magdalene Postel is a women’s religious congregation within the Roman Catholic Church founded by Saint Mary Magdalene Postel.
home.overviewdesc2: Julie Postel (1756–1846) was born in Barfleur, Normandy, in northern France. During the turbulent French Revolution, she secretly aided persecuted priests and educated poor children. Her congregation was founded in 1807 in Cherbourg. Together with Sr. Jeanne-Catherine Bellot, Sr. Louise Viel, and Sr. Angelique Ledanois, she took her religious vows and established a congregation dedicated to educating young people, instilling a love for God and a love for work, and selflessly helping the poor and alleviating the suffering of as many people as possible.
home.overviewdesc3: That was Julie Postel’s original vision and goal in founding a religious congregation.
home.quote: Living for God and serving others, especially those who are suffering
home.articledesc: Discover our community's spiritual programs and activities, designed to nourish faith and foster connection.
home.ctatitle: Would you like to join our mission?
home.ctadesc: I will go to the ends of the earth to seek out a single soul for Jesus Christ, even if, at the end of my journey, I face martyrdom.

charisma.title: Charisma
charisma.description: A calling to love, to glorify, and to embody the love of Christ
charisma.paragraph1: Living for God and serving others, especially those who suffer. That is the charism or gift of the Congregation: a call to love, glorify, and live out the love of Christ.
charisma.paragraph2: What I mean is, the sisters were called to…
charisma.point1Desc: To love God without limit and to do one’s utmost to ensure that He is loved.
charisma.point2Desc: Live to glorify God even more.
charisma.point3Desc: Our ongoing effort makes our lives truly lived by Jesus.
charisma.subtitle3: To be a servant to those who suffer
charisma.paragraph3: The Sisters of Saint Mary Magdalene Postel are soulmates to the sick, the poor, and the vulnerable. Their presence brings comfort and real hope to those who are marginalized in society. Through their sincere dedication to service, they demonstrate that compassion can be a source of strength for anyone struggling with life’s hardships.
charisma.quote: To live for God and to serve our neighbors, especially those in suffering.

history.title: History
history.subtitle: Seeds of a <highlight>Heart of Mercy</highlight> that Grow
history.paragraph1: The journey of compassion began with Julie Postel’s spirit of service, which grew through various challenges, sufferings, and hopes. That journey laid the foundation for the congregation we know today.
history.paragraph2: Join us in exploring the beautiful moments filled with struggle and sacrifice that have shaped our congregation.

birth.title: Birth of Julie Postel
birth.description: Born on November 28 in Barfleur, Northern France, as Julie Françoise Catherine Postel, the eldest of the Jean Postel le Vallois family. Her early aspiration was to dedicate herself to God by serving the poor.

firstCommunion.title: First Communion
firstCommunion.description: Received first communion at the age of 9, thanks to her exemplary behavior and outstanding qualities while attending the Benedictine sisters' boarding school in Valognes.

godmother.title: Becoming a Godmother
godmother.description: At the age of 12, she was asked to be a godmother for the baptisms of several babies.

valognesStudy.title: Education in Valognes
valognesStudy.description: Studied as a teacher for 6 years at the Benedictine sisters' school in Valognes, receiving a strong human and religious formation.

barfleur.title: Educational Ministry in Barfleur
barfleur.description: Opened schools and boarding schools for poor children. During the French Revolution, she helped a priest flee to England to save her priesthood and kept the Blessed Sacrament under a staircase.

cherbourg.title: Move to Cherbourg
cherbourg.description: On May 12, 1805, she left Barfleur for Cherbourg. There she opened a school and soon 3 young women joined her.

foundation.title: Vows Profession and Foundation of the Congregation
foundation.description: Thanks to her perseverance, the Church finally approved her vision. On September 8, 1807, she professed her vows alongside three companions, marking the official establishment of the Congregation.

octeville.title: Relocation to Octeville L’avenel
octeville.description: Cherbourg was left behind as the Sisters of Providence returned there. She then sought a new place in Octeville L’avenel, living inside a stable.

tamerville1.title: Tamerville
tamerville1.description: As Octeville L’avenel became inadequate, the group moved to Tamerville. Here the sisters took in 12 orphans, but jealousy towards their presence also began to emerge.

valognes.title: Valognes
valognes.description: Settled in Valognes, which could be likened to a deathbed house. However, she remained steadfast in continuing the struggle, even when advised to dissolve her congregation.

hamel.title: Move to Hamel au Bon
hamel.description: From Valognes she moved to Hamel au Bon, a thatched-roof cottage. It was here that she drafted the first Constitution amidst unceasing struggles.

tamerville2.title: Return to Tamerville
tamerville2.description: The sisters were called back to Tamerville. In order to be recognized by the royal government, the congregation had to find a motherhouse. Father Lerenard found a house for them.

abbaye.title: Settling in Saint-Sauveur-le-Vicomte (L’Abbaye)
abbaye.description: On June 7, 1832, the land purchase (L’Abbaye) was finalized, fulfilling Marie Rose Dadure's prophecy that a priest would lead her to L’Abbaye. On October 15, together with 14 sisters, she moved to this place until her death.

death.title: Passing of the Congregation's Founder
death.description: Passed away on July 16 at the age of 90, precisely on the Feast of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, after successfully preserving the congregation and settling in Saint-Sauveur-le-Vicomte.

canonization.title: Canonization as a Saint
canonization.description: Officially declared a saint by Pope Pius XI on May 24, 1925.

present.title: International Mission Expansion
present.description: The congregation’s spirit of compassion reaches every corner of the world through its ministry and work on various continents.

saints.title:
Three Saints of

Congregation
saints.subtitle: Model of Holiness and Dedication
saints.paragraph: The Congregation is built on a solid foundation of love and boundless devotion. We follow in the footsteps of the founder and the saints of the Congregation, emulating their virtues and exemplary lives as they dedicated themselves entirely to others and to the glory of God.

saint1.name: Saint Mary Magdalene Postel
saint1.description: The founder of the congregation was born Julie Postel. Amid the turmoil of the French Revolution, she secretly helped priests who were being hunted down by revolutionaries and taught poor children. In 1807, she founded this congregation with the primary focus of educating young people, instilling in them a love for God and a spirit of hard work, and selflessly dedicating herself to helping the poor and alleviating their suffering as much as possible. She led the community through difficult times of extreme poverty and succeeded in restoring the ancient monastery of Saint-Sauveur-le-Vicomte as the congregation’s center before passing away at the age of 89.
saint1.caption: The Sturdy Chêne Tree

saint2.name: Beata Placida Viel
saint2.description: She succeeded as the second Superior General of the congregation following the death of Saint Mary Magdalene Postel. Born Eulalie Victoire Jacqueline Viel, she was the niece and closest disciple of the founder. Under her calm and wise leadership, the congregation experienced rapid growth, received official recognition from the Holy See, and expanded its ministry beyond France, particularly to Germany.
saint2.caption: The Gentle Tilleul Tree

saint3.name: Beata Martha Le Bouteiller
saint3.description: A nun who lived out her holiness through the simplicity of her daily tasks at the Saint-Sauveur-le-Vicomte convent. Born Aimée Le Bouteiller, she spent nearly her entire religious life working hard in the kitchen, tending the garden, and managing the convent’s laundry. She was known for her obedience, humility, and perseverance in prayer amid a grueling routine of physical labor, without ever complaining.
saint3.caption: The Apple Tree that bears delicious fruit

spirituality.title: Spirituality
spirituality.subtitle: Spiritual Life, <highlight>Heart of Mercy</highlight>
spirituality.paragraph: To deeply appreciate the gift of their vocation, the Sisters of Saint Mary Magdalene Postel ground their lives in a spirituality of compassion. This spirit is embodied by following as closely as possible the person of Jesus Christ—who was poor and humbled—and by emulating His compassion toward humanity. The tangible expression of this commitment is reflected in their care, solidarity, sensitivity to the hardships of those who suffer, and sincere hospitality. Through humility, they are continually called to live out these virtues in their daily ministry.

practices.title: The True Character of Sister of Saint Mary Magdalene Postel

openness.title: Openness
openness.description: Open to changing times, adaptable, and receptive to feedback, ideas, and constructive criticism.

simplicity.title: Simplicity
simplicity.description: Authentic, free from grand ambitions, embracing a humble lifestyle.

poverty.title: Poverty
poverty.description: Feeling content, not being greedy, and not desiring material possessions excessively.

humility.title: Humility
humility.description: Eager to keep learning, aware of and accepting of one's own human limitations and frailties, appreciative of the gifts of others, and rich in the spirit of forgiveness.

spirituality.quote: You have given yourself to God; sacrifice it all. He desires not a part, but the whole of you.

services.title: Works of Ministry
services.description: I will go to the ends of the world to save a single soul for Christ
services.subtitle: Serving with a Tangible <highlight>Heart of Mercy</highlight>
services.paragraph1: Inspired by a passion for educating others and alleviating the suffering of their neighbors, the Sisters of St. Mary Magdalene Postel are called to manifest God’s generosity, compassion, and tenderness in the world by actively engaging in people’s lives and dedicating themselves to a wide variety of ministerial tasks, in order to show solidarity with the poor in all their forms.
services.paragraph2: As a tangible expression of the sisters’ commitment to alleviating the suffering of others, they actively participate in apostolic work in the fields of education, health, social services, and pastoral care. In carrying out their mission, the sisters take part in caring for the sick, teaching students in schools, and supporting the education of children who face financial difficulties in continuing their studies; they assist the poor, serve the elderly, accompany orphans, actively participate in various pastoral activities in parishes, and guide others who seek spiritual refreshment and deepening of their spirituality.
services.paragraph3: Through various means, the sisters bear witness through their lives to the presence and expansion of the Kingdom of God in their apostolic works.

healthcare.title: Healthcare
healthcare.tagline: HEAL THE BODY, TEND THE SOUL
healthcare.description: Caring for the sick is not an easy task, but the call to mission in this field opens the way to the mystery of God's glory. Compassion for the sick is a tangible expression of caring for Jesus in the wounded Samaritan.
healthcare.caption: Physical and Spiritual Healing

educational.title: Education
educational.description: In the midst of rapid intellectual advancement in our time, the suffering of students who drop out of school is a sorrow for the world. Sowing seeds of hope for the future of the youth rooted in God's love.
educational.caption: Guiding the Youth

social.title: Social
social.description: The radiance of a compassionate heart can transcend all our human limitations, fragility, and weaknesses. The dream of orphans to achieve independence is the deepest dream of our conscience.
social.caption: Embracing the Marginalized

pastoral.title: Pastoral
pastoral.description: The longing of every person's soul is to refresh the heart of anyone who thirsts for God's love. What we offer, whether in lack or abundance, is always sufficient to alleviate the unhappiness of our fellow beings.
pastoral.caption: Accompanying the Faithful

formation.title: Formation
formation.description: Formed in faith, rooted in prayer, and sent forth to serve.
formation.subtitle: Stages of Sisters' Formation
formation.paragraph1: The formation of the sisters follows its own program at each level. A sister goes through the stages of formation with the following progression:
formation.paragraph2: The aspects of formation carried out include:
formation.point3: Spirituality Formation of St. Mary Magdalene Postel

01.title: PRE-POSTULANCY
01.description: A young woman who is interested and desires to become a sister may be driven by various reasons and motivations, such as childhood dreams, admiration for the figure of a sister, fascination with a sister's 'attributes' (veil, crucifix necklace), and others. At this stage, the sympathizer's interest develops into curiosity and a desire to get to know and understand the daily life of the sisters (daily prayer activities, apostolic works, fraternity, etc.). Candidates experience a 'live-in' within several communities while getting to know and observing the sisters' lives and daily rhythms. The candidates undergo a 1-year aspirancy period. They wear ordinary clothes (skirts and blouses) and are given an identification badge featuring the Foundress, St. Mary Magdalene Postel.

02.title: POSTULANCY
02.description: Curiosity encourages the aspirant to take the step to 'GET TO KNOW' the congregation better. At this stage, the candidate begins to discover the spirit that motivates the sisters to choose this congregation, the history of the congregation, and the vision of its founders. The postulancy period lasts for 6 months. They wear the congregation's postulancy necklace.

03.title: NOVITIATE
03.description: At this stage, a postulant feels increasingly confident and dares to make a firm choice regarding the Congregation she is entering. A postulant is willing to take the next step into the novitiate stage, undergoing the initial education and training of a prospective sister. The candidate dares to decide to become a 'NEW MAN' (NEW PERSON), formed and guided to become a sister in accordance with the spirit/spirituality of the Congregation. A novice will undergo the novitiate stage for 2 years (1st-year and 2nd-year novice). Novices receive the Congregation necklace and the Constitution book.

04.title: JUNIORATE
04.description: After 2 years in the novitiate, a novice may submit a request to proceed to the next stage, namely First Vows (temporary vows). The novice will profess the evangelical counsels (three vows)—the vows of obedience, chastity, and poverty—meaning the novice promises to live solely for God within the Congregation by obeying superiors, living poorly, and remaining unmarried. The novices enter the juniorate period where they are sent out into the works of the Congregation. The juniorate period is undertaken by a sister until her fourth year, and in her fifth year, she is permitted to apply for perpetual vows. The maximum duration of temporary vows is up to 9 years, during which a junior sister must decide to proceed to Perpetual Vows or leave.

05.title: ONGOING FORMATION
05.description: After passing through the juniorate and professing perpetual vows, a sister's formation enters the Ongoing Formation stage. Sisters ranging from mid-senior to senior levels undergo ongoing formation stages to become increasingly integrated and deepened in all aspects of formation.

formation.paragraph3: Is your heart moved to answer God's call and live a consecrated life? Do not worry, you do not have to walk alone. Contact us anytime to talk about discerning God's will and starting the initial steps of formation.
